eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 4, Lesson 21
subtitle: Pulling exactly the rows and columns you need, in one line.

code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")

print(df["customer_name"].head(3))
print(df[["order_id", "product", "quantity"]].head(3))
caption: One column name returns a Series. A list of column names returns a smaller DataFrame — that extra bracket is the whole difference.

eyebrow: Boolean filtering: finding the real issue
code:
negative_qty = df[df["quantity"] < 0]
print(negative_qty)

#    order_id  customer_name  quantity  ...
# 13     1014   Marcus Ibeh        -1  ...
caption: df["quantity"] < 0 produces a True/False Series — passing it back into df[...] keeps only the True rows.
Each condition needs its own parentheses — leaving them off is a common source of confusing errors.

code:
df_indexed = df.set_index("order_id")
print(df_indexed.loc[1005])

# customer_name    NaN
# region          West
# product  Camp Stove Duo
# ...
caption: set_index makes .loc[1005] mean "the row labeled 1005" — not row number 1005. NaN here is pandas' missing-value marker.
